Numeric values and total count of cpuhp_state members beyond the invalid, offline, and dynamic window sizes.
Enabled cpuidle selection, entry, registration, and governor algorithms; only the disabled fallback is visible.
Broadcast timer coordination, coupled barrier protocol, and sysfs object lifetimes for idle devices and drivers.
Power notifier effects, low level idle body, per processor tick handling, and clock event constraints beyond the stated prohibitions.

findings.text: Processor bringup and teardown progress through ordered phases. A sentinel marks invalid, offline anchors the start, early preparation runs on a managing processor, then a kick hands control to the arriving processor, low level starting steps run locally, the threaded online section follows, and active plus online mark completion. Teardown walks the same order in reverse, with dying and dead markers interleaved for services that must stop early or late.

CPUHP_INVALID equals negative one and CPUHP_OFFLINE equals zero. The early preparation dynamic range spans twenty entries past its base and the threaded online dynamic range spans forty entries past its base. The dummy timer starting entry is ordered after all other timer starting entries.

Single shot registration associates a phase identifier and a human readable label with a bringup callback and a teardown callback, each receiving a processor number and reporting status. One form invokes callbacks for processors already present, a nocalls form skips those invocations, and cpuslocked forms require the caller to already hold processor set protection.

Multi instance registration associates a phase and label with callbacks that additionally receive a list node identifying the affected instance. Instances are managed separately after registration, and initial invocation for existing processors is suppressed in this form.

For multi instance phases, separate helpers add or remove one list node at a time. Variants select whether callbacks for the transition run immediately and whether the caller already holds processor set protection, with return status reporting acceptance.

Removal helpers detach a previously registered phase. Single instance removal can optionally invoke teardown for present processors, while nocalls and multi forms skip those invocations. Locked variants assume the caller already holds processor set protection.

Bringup callbacks run while moving toward online and teardown callbacks run while moving toward offline for the same phase. Both receive only the affected processor number in the single instance form, so per phase state must be looked up elsewhere.
In this configuration the online idle marker, the dead reporting hook, and the architecture dead cleanup hook are present but perform no action and take no decisions.

Processor set protection offers shared read acquisition, exclusive write acquisition, plus matching releases, a nonblocking read attempt that reports success, and assertions for held state. Separate controls can pause offlining or fully disable and reenable hotplug transitions. In this view all of these are inert shims that always report held or successful.
Processor removal is refused with a permission failure in this configuration, and the helper that would stop secondary processors during shutdown performs no action.
Each idle driver supports at most ten states. State names hold up to sixteen characters and descriptions hold up to thirty two characters, including termination in the usual C sense.

Per state disable tracking uses one bit for user requests and a second bit for driver requests. State behavior flags distinguish polling, coupled multi processor scope, tick stopped while idle, administrative unusable and default off markers, plus notices that entry flushes address translations or already handles quiescent grace handling.

The per state accounting record holds counters for disable events and entries, accumulated residency time, counts of too deep versus too shallow selections, rejected entry attempts, and when suspend to idle is configured additional usage and time counters for that path.

An idle state descriptor carries a name and description, exit latency and minimum residency expressed in both nanosecond and microsecond forms, behavior flags, a power estimate, and three entry hooks for normal entry, entry on a dying processor, and entry with timekeeping suspended.

A per processor idle device records registration and enable markers, a poll limit marker, processor identity, a wake timer handle, last state choice with last residency, poll and latency limits, an array of per state accounting records sized by the maximum, sysfs linkage, a global list node, and optional coupled set membership when that option is enabled.

An idle driver carries a name and owner, a broadcast timer marker, a fixed capacity array of state descriptors, a populated count, a safe fallback index, a mask of covered processors, and a preferred governor name.

A governor descriptor carries a name, list linkage, a rating, enable and disable hooks taking driver and device, a selection hook that may request tick suppression, and a reflect hook that observes the chosen state for learning.

Populated driver states must appear with highest draw first and lowest last. The safe index provides a fallback when deeper states are unavailable, the broadcast marker requests timer framework coordination, and the mask defines which processors the driver manages.

Idle entry is a paired bracket around low level idle that may temporarily permit interrupts. It may only be used when interrupts are already disabled and it coordinates tracing visibility, instrumentation boundaries, context tracking idle marking, and lock tracking irq state so that exit restores a consistent disabled view.

The suspend to idle entry path runs with per processor tick or whole timekeeping stopped, so it must never reenable interrupts even briefly and must not alter clock event devices. Sharing the normal entry implementation is allowed only when those constraints already hold.

When idle support is compiled out, registration and selection helpers report missing device, lookup helpers return null, poll time returns zero, availability checks report unavailable, and pause, resume, reflect, disable and unregister helpers perform no action.

Suspend to idle helpers offer deepest state search under a latency bound, direct entry under a latency bound, and a sticky selection of the deepest allowed state. In this configuration the search and entry report missing device and the sticky selector does nothing.

Power management idle wrappers provide a unified contract with options for retention and for caller managed quiescence, plus an optional separate state argument. A zero index requests the shallowest path, retention requests omit power notifications, caller managed quiescence omits idle tracking, and the outcome distinguishes success by returning the requested index from failure by returning a negative sentinel.

Coupled states affect more than one processor and require cross processor coordination before entry. Timer stop states run without periodic tick support, address translation flush states imply extra resume cost, and quiescence aware states take responsibility that would otherwise need explicit idle tracking.

Processor set size derives from either a build time maximum or a runtime count depending on configuration, with small and large variants selecting the appropriate bound and a common alias for the runtime count. Six global read only views expose possible, online, enabled, present, active, and dying sets.

First set, first clear, first intersection, and first difference queries each scan from the start up to the small bound and return the lowest matching processor index, delegating bit search to helpers owned elsewhere.

The runtime processor count setter warns when a single processor build or forced count configuration receives a mismatched value and otherwise stores the supplied count. Print formatting for masks pairs the runtime count with a pointer to the underlying bits.

One configuration reads the current processor idle device through per processor storage, while the disabled configuration returns null for both device and driver lookups. Poll state initialization and the coupled parallel barrier are present but inert in this view.

Calling selection, entry, or play dead paths while idle support is unavailable must be treated as an error rather than an idle transition, since they report missing device and perform no power action.

Idle pause helpers provide a locking form that suspends selection while held and a plain form for contexts that already serialize callers, with matching resume helpers to restore operation. In this configuration all four are inert.
